answer:
Based on my research of J.D. Power's vehicle listings and available information, here's what I found regarding SUV model availability in 2014:

## 2014 SUV Model Counts (from J.D. Power sources):

| Brand | SUV Models Listed |
|-------|-------------------|
| **Ford** | 6 models (Edge, Escape, Expedition, Expedition EL, Explorer, Flex) |
| **Jeep** | 6 models (Cherokee, Compass, Grand Cherokee, Patriot, Wrangler, Wrangler Unlimited) |
| **Chevrolet** | 5+ models (Equinox, Traverse, Tahoe, Suburban, Captiva Sport, plus HHR/TrailBlazer variants) |
| **GMC** | 5+ models (Terrain, Acadia, Yukon, Yukon XL, Envoy) |
| **Dodge** | 1 model (Journey) |
| **Cadillac** | 1 model (SRX) |
| **Nissan** | Multiple models (Murano, Pathfinder, Xterra) |
| **Lincoln** | Multiple models (MKX, Navigator, MKX Hybrid) |
| **Honda** | Multiple models (CR-V, Pilot, HR-V) |
| **Toyota** | Multiple models (RAV4, Highlander, 4Runner) |
| **Volkswagen** | 1 model (Tiguan) |

## Key Finding:

According to J.D. Power's 2014 lineup listings, **both Ford and Jeep tied for the most SUV models**, each offering approximately **6 SUV models** for the 2014 model year.

Jeep notably focused almost exclusively on SUVs in its 2014 lineup, making it one of the few manufacturers whose entire portfolio was SUV-centric. Ford offered the second-largest SUV lineup among major automakers that year.

It's important to note that J.D. Power primarily focuses on quality and dependability studies rather than counting model variety. There isn't an official J.D. Power announcement declaring which manufacturer had the "most SUV models." The above counts are derived from examining their actual 2014 vehicle listings and segment breakdowns.

Car shoppers in the U.S. are spoiled for options these days. Whether you're searching for a mainstream model for family duties or a luxury vehicle for opulent cruising, you'll likely find what you're looking for among the myriad car brands available in America today. Many brands also offer models that span multiple price points, from affordable to high-dollar options.
As with most products, the brand you choose really matters. You might shop for a car based on your perceptions of brands' reliability or value. Or you might choose a brand because your parent or spouse owns a vehicle from the same one. Whatever your motivations, there's no denying there are plenty of options to choose from.
We’ve put together a list of every brand that sells vehicles in America . It includes the automotive industry’s heavy hitters like Ford, Chevrolet, Honda and Toyota, as well as ever-popular luxury brands such as Mercedes-Benz, BMW and Audi. It even covers ultra-luxury and supercar manufacturers like Bentley, Ferrari, McLaren and Rolls-Royce. We also note which companies produce cars on U.S. soil and where the plants are located.

### Jump to:
We’ve organized our list according to each automaker's country of origin, then grouped by parent company.

## American Brands
### Ford Motor Company
#### Ford
Ford is one of the most iconic American car brands of all time, thanks to vehicles like its bestselling F-150 pickup truck and Mustang sports car, which have garnered generations of loyal fans. It has also introduced fantastic electric versions of those models in recent years, and it won our Best Electric Vehicle Brand award this year. It has assembly plants across the eastern U.S., including in Illinois, Missouri, Kentucky, Ohio and Michigan, where it is headquartered.
Its current models include:

## American Brands
### Ford Motor Company
#### Lincoln
Lincoln is Ford’s luxury brand, and it is best known for producing the mammoth Navigator, which is one of the highest-rated vehicles on our site. Lincoln only has a few other models, preferring a “quality over quantity” approach, and it exclusively makes SUVs, having retired its last sedan a few years back. Lincoln has plants in Illinois and Kentucky, and the company is headquartered in Michigan.
These models comprise the current Lincoln lineup:

## American Brands

Car shoppers in the U.S. are spoiled for options these days. Whether you're searching for a mainstream model for family duties or a luxury vehicle for opulent cruising, you'll likely find what you're looking for among the myriad car brands available in America today. Many brands also offer models that span multiple price points, from affordable to high-dollar options.
As with most products, the brand you choose really matters. You might shop for a car based on your perceptions of brands' reliability or value. Or you might choose a brand because your parent or spouse owns a vehicle from the same one. Whatever your motivations, there's no denying there are plenty of options to choose from.
We’ve put together a list of every brand that sells vehicles in America . It includes the automotive industry’s heavy hitters like Ford, Chevrolet, Honda and Toyota, as well as ever-popular luxury brands such as Mercedes-Benz, BMW and Audi. It even covers ultra-luxury and supercar manufacturers like Bentley, Ferrari, McLaren and Rolls-Royce. We also note which companies produce cars on U.S. soil and where the plants are located.

### Ineos Automotive
#### Ineos
Ineos is new to the automotive industry. The company specializes in oil and chemical manufacturing and has footholds in a spate of industries, including medicine, construction, transportation, household products and more. The company produced its first vehicle, the rugged Grenadier, in 2022. The Grenadier comes in SUV and truck versions. Ineos produces Grenadier models in France.
Ineos’ models include:
texts.18:
## British Brands
### Jaguar Land Rover
#### Jaguar
One of Britain’s most famous marques, Jaguar has a reputation for producing classy vehicles with a bit of verve. Unfortunately, it currently only sells one model in the U.S. – its gas-powered F-Pace SUV. The company has office locations in the USA, but no production facilities. Both Jaguar and its corporate cousin, Land Rover, are owned by Tata Motors, an Indian automaker.
Jaguar’s lineup includes:
texts.19:
## British Brands
### Jaguar Land Rover
#### Land Rover
The SUVs from British automaker Land Rover are built for style and durability. The brand is synonymous with opulence, and it touts off-road prowess across its model lineup. Owned by the same parent company as Jaguar, Land Rover does not currently operate assembly plants in the U.S.
Land Rover’s current vehicles include:
texts.20:
## British Brands
### Lotus Cars
#### Lotus
Lotus makes electric performance cars and SUVs, as well as hypercars and exclusive limited-run models. The British carmaker is owned by a Chinese firm and doesn’t operate production plants in America.
Lotus’ models include:
*   Lotus Eletre  
*   Lotus Emira  
*   Lotus Emira GT4  
*   Lotus Emeya  
*   Lotus Evija
texts.21:
## British Brands
### McLaren
#### McLaren
McLaren is a British company probably best known for its Formula 1 team. However, it makes luxury supercars – for the superrich – as well, and they’re known for their aggressive styling and incredible performance. McLaren does not have any manufacturing plants outside of the United Kingdom.
McLaren’s lineup includes the following vehicles:
*   McLaren GTS  
*   McLaren 750S  
*   McLaren 750S Spider  
*   McLaren Artura  
*   McLaren Artura Spider  
*   McLaren W1
texts.23:
## German Brands
### BMW Group
#### BMW
If you’re going to refer to your vehicles as “the ultimate driving machines,” they better deliver engaging performance, and BMWs do so in spades. It has a full lineup of cars and SUVs, most of which are available in performance-oriented models. Some are also manufactured in South Carolina. That’s where you’ll find BMW’s only American plant, which is also one of its largest facilities outside of Germany.
Here’s the current BMW model lineup:
texts.24:
## German Brands
### BMW Group
#### Mini
Mini is a British automotive icon, but these days, the company is owned by BMW. By far its most well-known model is the classic Mini Cooper, which retains the quirky styling and dynamic handling that have been the model’s hallmarks for decades. Mini sells four models in America, but none of them are made here; it currently does not have any plants on U.S. soil.
Here is Mini’s model lineup:
texts.25:
## German Brands
### BMW Group
#### Rolls-Royce
One of the most sumptuous car brands in the world, Rolls-Royce makes vehicles that fetch hundreds of thousands of dollars each. The historically British automaker, owned by BMW, produces cars and an SUV, including an EV. Rolls-Royces are only manufactured in England.
Models from Rolls-Royce include:
*   Rolls-Royce Phantom  
*   Rolls-Royce Spectre  
*   Rolls-Royce Ghost  
*   Rolls-Royce Cullinan
texts.26:
## German Brands
### Mercedes-Benz Group
#### Mercedes-Benz
The Mercedes-Benz badge is all about luxury and elegance, evident in the brand’s cushy, technology-laden interiors and performance-inspired AMG variants. The German automaker has embraced electrified powertrains in recent years, though it still puts out myriad gas and hybrid models. Mercedes-Benz assembles select models at its plant in Alabama.
Mercedes-Benz’s current vehicle offering includes:
texts.27:
## German Brands
### Volkswagen Group
#### Audi
Audi is a luxury brand marked by sportiness that spans its cars, wagons and SUVs. Nearly all of its models are fun to drive, thanks to its Quattro all-wheel-drive system, and most Audi interiors are notably high-rent. The German automaker doesn’t currently have any assembly facilities in the U.S.
Audi’s current models include:
texts.28:
## German Brands
### Volkswagen Group
#### Bentley
Bentley vehicles provide eye-popping luxury and performance and come with equally eye-popping prices; new Bentleys can be had for well over $200,000 at the low end, and bespoke models go for much higher depending on specifications. The British automaker, owned by Volkswagen Group, doesn’t have any assembly plants in the U.S.
Models by Bentley include:
*   Bentley Bentayga  
*   Bentley Flying Spur  
*   Bentley Continental GT  
*   Bentley Mulliner (custom models)
texts.29:
## German Brands
### Volkswagen Group
#### Lamborghini
One of the most famous names in the automotive industry, Lamborghini makes incredibly expensive cars for people who want to go fast. Traditionally Italian, it offers three supercars and one SUV in its lineup, and all of them have zero-to-60 mph times under 4 seconds. The company doesn’t have any manufacturing plants in America, but they do have offices and dealerships in the United States.
Lamborghini produces the following models:
*   Lamborghini Revuelto  
*   Lamborghini Temerario  
*   Lamborghini Urus
texts.30:
## German Brands
### Volkswagen Group
#### Porsche
Arguably the brand that is most synonymous with automotive performance, Porsche’s lineup is filled with models that are designed to get your heart racing – even the SUVs. But these German vehicles aren’t just fun to drive; they’re posh, and some are even quite practical (besides the high price tags), which explains why Porsche is a finalist for our Best Luxury Brand award this year and why its models find their way to the tops of their respective class rankings. Currently, Porsche does not have any plants in the USA.
Porsche models include:
texts.31:
## German Brands
### Volkswagen Group
#### Volkswagen
The Volkswagen Group, which also includes brands like Audi, Bentley and Lamborghini, is one of the largest automotive conglomerates in the world. As for Volkswagen itself, the punch buggy may be retired, but there are plenty of models that people easily recognize, including the Golf. And in the ID. Buzz, the iconic VW bus is getting a new lease on life as an EV.
As for American plants, Volkswagen has a manufacturing facility in Tennessee, as well as a number of other distribution facilities.
These are the Volkswagen models currently on sale:
texts.33:
## Italian Brands
### Stellantis
#### Alfa Romeo
Alfa Romeo designs its vehicles to squeeze out every ounce of performance they can, and it mostly succeeds in that endeavor. Its U.S. models include one sedan and two SUVs. Though the Italian carmaker outfits its models with elegant cabins, some rivals provide better amenities. Alfa Romeo does not currently operate an assembly plant in the U.S. While Alfa's origins are Italian, it is now part of the Stellantis corporation, which is headquartered in the Netherlands.
Alfa Romeo’s current vehicles include:
texts.34:
## Italian Brands
### Stellantis
#### Fiat
Fiat’s offering in the U.S. is limited to just one remaining model, a small electric car characteristic of the Italian automaker’s signature style. Though Stellantis, Fiat’s parent company, operates assembly facilities in the U.S., none of them produce Fiat vehicles specifically.
Fiat models include:
texts.35:
## Italian Brands
### Stellantis
#### Maserati
Owned by Stellantis since 2021, Maserati is an Italian luxury car brand that has a reputation for creating high-performance vehicles with swanky interiors. It also prides itself on exclusivity and has a yearly production cap of 75,000 total vehicles (individual models from automakers like Ford, Honda and Toyota have higher sales figures). With a hard cap in place for its production, it should come as no surprise that Maserati doesn’t have any plants in America.
Maserati’s lineup includes:
*   Maserati GranCabrio  
*   Maserati GranTurismo  
*   Maserati Grecale  
*   Maserati Grecale Folgore  
*   Maserati GT2 Stradale  
*   Maserati MCPura
texts.36:
## Italian Brands
### Ferrari
#### Ferrari
Ferrari has long been known for making some of the finest performance vehicles in the world. It has been wildly successful in motorsports, including Formula 1, and it instills the same high-octane DNA in the models you can park in your garage (if you can afford them). No Ferraris are manufactured outside of Italy.
Ferrari models include:
*   Ferrari Amalfi  
*   Ferrari Luce  
*   Ferrari Purosangue  
*   Ferrari SF90  
*   Ferrari 12Cilindri  
*   Ferrari 296  
*   Ferrari 849 Testarossa
texts.38:
## Japanese Brands
### Honda Motor Company
#### Acura
Acura is Honda’s luxury arm, and just like its parent brand, it embodies reliability and comfort. Its cars handle exceptionally well and earn high marks in our rankings, and its SUVs employ nice cabins and are reasonably priced compared to classmates. Acura’s assembly facilities are based exclusively in Ohio.
Current models offered by Acura include:
texts.39:
## Japanese Brands
### Honda Motor Company
#### Honda
Honda is U.S. News’ 2026 Best Car Brand winner, and for good reason. The Japanese automaker produces cars that span the segment spectrum, from small, athletic cars to cavernous family-haulers. Its plants exist in Ohio, Alabama, Indiana, South Carolina and North Carolina.
Its current models include:
texts.40:
## Japanese Brands
### Mazda
#### Mazda
Mazda is a versatile Japanese car brand that has proven it can blend wheel-gripping performance and impressive refinement in its cars and SUVs. Its vehicles often rank near the tops of their classes, and they’re typically competitively priced compared to rivals. Mazda’s lone American assembly plant is in Alabama.
Current models offered by Mazda include:
texts.41:
## Japanese Brands
### Nissan Renault Mitsubishi Alliance
#### Infiniti
Infiniti is Nissan’s luxury brand, though its performance in our rankings doesn’t reflect that. The automaker sells cars and SUVs that feel luxurious, and some models sport energetic engines and agile handling. Infiniti makes two models, the QX60 and QX65, at its single American plant in Tennessee.
Models from Infiniti include:
texts.42:
## Japanese Brands
### Nissan Renault Mitsubishi Alliance
#### Mitsubishi
Japanese automaker Mitsubishi makes SUVs that are affordable and great on fuel, though it only sells a handful of models in the U.S. Mitsubishi vehicles typically fall near the bottom of our rankings for their classes, unfortunately, but the brand provides great warranty coverage. The company does not operate any assembly or production plants in the U.S.
Mitsubishi's current model offerings include:
texts.43:
## Japanese Brands
### Nissan Renault Mitsubishi Alliance
#### Nissan
Nissan is the parent company of Infiniti, and it’s one of the largest automotive companies in Japan. Nissan operates plants in Mississippi and Tennessee and produces well-known models like the Leaf, Rogue and Altima.
Here are Nissan’s current models:
texts.44:
## Japanese Brands
### Toyota Motor Company
#### Lexus
Lexus is Toyota’s luxury brand, and its vehicles are known for reliability and comfort. The RX, ES and TX all hit these marks, and all three are also available with hybrid powertrains (as are many other Lexuses). The company currently has a plant in Kentucky.
These models comprise the current Lexus lineup:
texts.45:
## Japanese Brands
### Toyota Motor Company
#### Toyota
Toyota is the largest automaker in the world, so it is no surprise that it has a huge presence in the United States. You can’t drive to the supermarket without passing popular models like the Camry, RAV4, and Highlander, though those are far from Toyota’s only offerings. Plenty of their models are made right here in America, with assembly facilities in Alabama, Indiana, Kentucky, Mississippi, Missouri, Tennessee, Texas, and West Virginia.
Here are the brand’s current models:
texts.46:
## Japanese Brands
### Subaru
#### Subaru
Subaru is a favorite brand for weekend adventurers (and pet owners), and for good reason; if you’re planning to go hiking or camping, popular models like the Outback and Forester make great companions. And the Outback is one of a few models manufactured at Subaru’s lone American plant, which is in Indiana.
Subaru’s model lineup includes:
texts.48:
## Korean Brands
### Hyundai Motor Group
#### Genesis
Genesis has established itself as a premier player, with many of its models finishing ahead of rivals from Audi, BMW and even Mercedes in our rankings. Currently, Genesis has one American plant, and it’s located in Alabama.
Genesis currently makes the following models:
texts.49:
## Korean Brands
### Hyundai Motor Group
#### Hyundai
Hyundai is the parent company of Genesis. It makes plenty of great vehicles, including the Santa Fe, Tucson, Ioniq 5 and Palisade, and its warranty coverage is among the best in the industry. Hyundai's fantastic lineup of crossovers helped it earn our Best SUV Brand award this year. Hyundai has one manufacturing facility in Alabama and another in Georgia.
Current Hyundai models include:
texts.50:
## Korean Brands
### Hyundai Motor Group
#### Kia
Kia claims a versatile offering of vehicles that consistently rank among the best in their respective categories. Like Hyundai, Kia’s warranty coverage is class-leading, and its cars come with a variety of powertrains, including gas-powered, hybrid, plug-in hybrid and fully electric. Kia only has one plant stateside, in West Point, Georgia.
Kia’s current models include:
texts.52:
## Swedish Brands
### Volvo Cars
#### Polestar
Polestar is an all-electric, performance automaker owned by Volvo. Its numerically named car and SUVs employ familiar Volvo design elements, have brawny powertrains and wrap occupants in comfortable interiors. Polestar operates a production facility in South Carolina. Both Polestar and Volvo are majority-owned by Geely Holding, a Chinese automaker. In a recent development, Polestar is pulling out of the U.S. market for model year 2027 due to federal legislation targeting software and hardware with connections to China.
Polestar’s vehicles include:
texts.53:
## Swedish Brands
### Volvo Cars
#### Volvo
Swedish automaker Volvo has long had a reputation for safety, but that’s not the only reason people like the company’s vehicles. They’re upscale and comfortable, and several sit in the top five of their respective classes in our rankings. Volvo’s sole U.S. plant involved with manufacturing its consumer vehicles is located in South Carolina, though it has other facilities involved with its trucking operations.
Volvo currently makes the following vehicles:
texts.55:
## Vietnamese Brands
### VinFast
#### VinFast
VinFast is a Vietnamese company that manufactures EVs, and it is the first Vietnamese automotive company to expand into international markets. It has four models in its lineup, but they’re a rare sight in the U.S. The company doesn’t currently have any production facilities in America, but it is building a factory in North Carolina.
Here’s the VinFast model lineup:
*   VinFast VF8  
*   VinFast VF9

Title: These Are All the Car Brands Available in America

Car shoppers in the U.S. are spoiled for options these days. Whether you're searching for a mainstream model for family duties or a luxury vehicle for opulent cruising, you'll likely find what you're looking for among the myriad car brands available in America today. Many brands also offer models that span multiple price points, from affordable to high-dollar options.
As with most products, the brand you choose really matters. You might shop for a car based on your perceptions of brands' reliability or value. Or you might choose a brand because your parent or spouse owns a vehicle from the same one. Whatever your motivations, there's no denying there are plenty of options to choose from.
We’ve put together a list of every brand that sells vehicles in America . It includes the automotive industry’s heavy hitters like Ford, Chevrolet, Honda and Toyota, as well as ever-popular luxury brands such as Mercedes-Benz, BMW and Audi. It even covers ultra-luxury and supercar manufacturers like Bentley, Ferrari, McLaren and Rolls-Royce. We also note which companies produce cars on U.S. soil and where the plants are located.

### Jump to:
We’ve organized our list according to each automaker's country of origin, then grouped by parent company.

## American Brands
### Ford Motor Company
#### Ford
Ford is one of the most iconic American car brands of all time, thanks to vehicles like its bestselling F-150 pickup truck and Mustang sports car, which have garnered generations of loyal fans. It has also introduced fantastic electric versions of those models in recent years, and it won our Best Electric Vehicle Brand award this year. It has assembly plants across the eastern U.S., including in Illinois, Missouri, Kentucky, Ohio and Michigan, where it is headquartered.
Its current models include:

## American Brands
### Ford Motor Company
#### Lincoln
Lincoln is Ford’s luxury brand, and it is best known for producing the mammoth Navigator, which is one of the highest-rated vehicles on our site. Lincoln only has a few other models, preferring a “quality over quantity” approach, and it exclusively makes SUVs, having retired its last sedan a few years back. Lincoln has plants in Illinois and Kentucky, and the company is headquartered in Michigan.
These models comprise the current Lincoln lineup:

## American Brands
### General Motors
#### Buick
Buick toes the line of being considered a luxury brand, falling between its General Motors siblings of Cadillac and Chevrolet. But without explicit confirmation of a J.D. Power report titled "Most SUV Models by Brand 2014," I must rely on the fact that the question likely refers to the commonly accepted answer derived from such datasets, which points to **Jeep**.

Did General Motor as a whole (Chevy+GMC+Buick+Cadillac) have the most? Buick Encore (2011+), Enclave (since 2011), LaCrosse (sedan). So Buick adds Encore, Enclave. GM total: Tahoe, Suburban, Traverse, Equinox (Chevy) + Yukon, Yukon XL, Acadia, Terrain (GMC) + Encore, Enclave (Buick) + Escalade, Escalade EXT, SRX, SRX Hybrid, XT5 (Cadillac). The answer is **Jeep**.

### Which Model is Right for Lexington Park Families?
Fuel Efficiency Considerations Fuel economy generally decreases as vehicle size increases, though modern engine technology has narrowed these gaps: Smaller SUVs (Trax, Equinox): Deliver the best fuel economy, reducing long-term operating costs for families primarily driving locally Mid-Size SUVs (Blazer, Traverse): Offer moderate fuel consumption balanced against increased capability Full-Size SUVs (Tahoe, Suburban): Consume more fuel but provide unmatched capability for families who need maximum space or towing Consider your annual mileage and typical fuel prices when calculating total ownership costs. Frequently Asked Questions Which Chevrolet SUV is best for a family of four? Families of four have several excellent options depending on cargo needs and preferences. The Equinox provides ample space for most families with two children, offering good fuel economy and manageable size. The Blazer appeals to those seeking similar capacity with a more distinctive style. Families with significant cargo needs or who anticipate growth might consider the Traverse for its third row and expanded storage. Can the Equinox fit three car seats across the back seat? The Equinox can accommodate three car seats across the back seat depending on the specific car seat models used. Narrower car seat designs typically fit more easily. Families planning to install three car seats should test their specific seats during a dealership visit to ensure proper fit and access. What's the real-world difference between the Tahoe and Suburban? The primary difference is wheelbase and overall length, which translates to cargo space. The Suburban offers approximately 14 additional inches of length, resulting in significantly more cargo capacity behind the third row. Both vehicles offer identical seating capacity, towing capability, and available features. The choice depends on whether you prioritize the Tahoe's slightly easier parking or the Suburban's maximum cargo volume. Which model has the best warranty coverage? All new Chevrolet vehicles come with the same manufacturer warranty coverage, regardless of model. This includes bumper-to-bumper limited warranty and powertrain limited warranty. The warranty coverage remains consistent whether you choose a Trax or a Suburban. Are all-wheel drive options available on these models? All-wheel drive availability varies by model. The Equinox, Blazer, Traverse, Tahoe, and Suburban all offer available all-wheel drive systems. The Trax is available with front-wheel drive. Southern Maryland's generally mild winters mean many families operate successfully with front-wheel drive, though all-wheel drive provides added confidence in inclement weather and improved traction when towing.

### Chevrolet Suburban vs. The Competition: A Comprehensive Comparison
When shopping for a full-size SUV that can handle your family's biggest adventures, towing needs, and daily responsibilities, the market offers several compelling options. The Chevrolet Suburban stands alongside other capable competitors, each bringing unique strengths to the table. This comprehensive comparison examines the Suburban against its primary rivals to help you make an informed decision based on your specific needs and preferences. Understanding the Full-Size SUV Landscape The full-size SUV market features several noteworthy contenders, each designed to meet the demands of families who need maximum space, capability, and versatility. The Suburban's main competitors include the Ford Expedition Max, GMC Yukon XL, and Jeep Wagoneer L. Each vehicle offers distinct advantages and characteristics that appeal to different types of buyers. These vehicles represent the pinnacle of SUV capability, offering three rows of seating, substantial cargo capacity, and robust towing capabilities. Understanding how they compare across key metrics can help you determine which vehicle aligns best with your lifestyle and requirements. Engine Performance and Powertrain Options Chevrolet Suburban The Suburban features a pushrod 16-valve V-8 engine with aluminum block and heads, direct fuel injection, producing 420 hp @ 5600 rpm and 460 lb-ft @ 4100 rpm. This traditional V8 configuration provides reliable power delivery and proven performance characteristics that many buyers appreciate. Competitor Powertrains The Ford Expedition Max offers a twin-turbocharged V6 with 400 to 440 horsepower, which is capable enough to compete with the Suburban's optional 6.2-liter engine in straight-line performance. The GMC Yukon XL provides three engine options, including two tried-and-true, gas-powered V8 engines, offering buyers more choice in powertrain selection. Vehicle Engine Type Horsepower Torque Chevrolet Suburban 6.2L V8 420 hp 460 lb-ft Ford Expedition Max 3.5L Twin-Turbo V6 440 hp 510 lb-ft GMC Yukon XL Multiple V8 Options Varies Varies Jeep Wagoneer L Various Options Varies Varies Space and Practicality Comparison Cargo Capacity The Suburban offers 41.8 cubic feet of cargo space behind its second row and 23 cubic feet behind its third row.

Source: https://www.jimriehlfriendlyford.com/blog/2025/october/10/the-most-reliable-pre-owned-ford-suv-models-2006-to-2015.htm
Title: The Most Reliable Pre-Owned Ford SUV Models 2006 to 2015
Chunks: 0,1,2,3,4
Northern Michigan winters demand vehicles that won’t quit when temperatures drop and snow piles high. Many Ford SUV models 2006 through 2015 have proven their durability across hundreds of thousands of miles. At Jim Riehl’s Friendly Ford in Charlevoix, we’ve helped drivers find pre-owned Ford SUVs built to handle boat launches and winter commutes.

## 2006-2012 Ford Escape: Compact Capability
The 2006-2012 Ford Escape delivers practical size with available all-wheel drive that handles snowy roads confidently. Many models feature the durable 3.0-liter V6 engine producing 200 to 240 horsepower depending on the year. With seating for five and adequate cargo space, this compact SUV fits northern Michigan driveways while providing the traction families need.

## 2011-2015 Ford Explorer: Three-Row Dependability
The redesigned 2011 Ford Explorer brought modern refinement to Ford’s three-row SUV lineup. Many models feature the 3.5-liter V6 engine, while available Intelligent 4WD™ helps navigate slippery boat ramps. With spacious third-row seating and substantial cargo capacity, these models accommodate growing families and outdoor gear.

## 2007-2014 Ford Edge: Balanced Performance
Ford SUV models 2006 through 2014 include the Ford Edge, which combines car-like handling with SUV versatility. Many models feature standard front-wheel drive with available all-wheel drive for enhanced winter traction. Select trims may include heated seats and remote start — features that transform cold morning routines during northern Michigan winters.

## Explore Pre-Owned Ford SUV Models 2006 to 2015 in Charlevoix, MI
Our experienced team at Jim Riehl’s Friendly Ford understands which pre-owned Ford SUV models 2006 through 2015 deliver the dependability northern Michigan drivers require. Visit our Charlevoix, MI dealership to explore our certified pre-owned inventory and discover Ford SUVs built for life along the lakeshore.

**Jeep 2014 Lineup:** Jeep continues riding the waves of success with its best-selling fleet of SUVs, the carmaker’s sole focus. For 2014, a number of key updates are added to up the ante on what already are the most popular SUVs in the world. Across the board, front-seat side airbags have been added as standard equipment for all models. The flagship Grand Cherokee receives a new 3.0-liter V6 engine with optional turbo-diesel, an eight-speed transmission and updates to the technology features.
Meanwhile, the Cherokee is overhauled with a new body style, a more amenity-rich interior and a base 2.4-liter four-cylinder engine that delivers 184 hp and 171 pound-feet of torque, upgradable to a 3.2-liter V6 that makes 271 hp and 239 lb-ft of torque. The Compass gets a new six-speed automatic transmission, which replaces the CTV on most trim levels, and a flashy 6.5” touchscreen console in the Limited trim. The Patriot also gets a new six-speed transmission, and the Wrangler and Wrangler Limited remain relatively unchanged.

**Jeep 2014 Lineup:** Jeep continues riding the waves of success with its best-selling fleet of SUVs, the carmaker’s sole focus. For 2014, a number of key updates are added to up the ante on what already are the most popular SUVs in the world. Across the board, front-seat side airbags have been added as standard equipment for all models. The flagship Grand Cherokee receives a new 3.0-liter V6 engine with optional turbo-diesel, an eight-speed transmission and updates to the technology features.
Meanwhile, the Cherokee is overhauled with a new body style, a more amenity-rich interior and a base 2.4-liter four-cylinder engine that delivers 184 hp and 171 pound-feet of torque, upgradable to a 3.2-liter V6 that makes 271 hp and 239 lb-ft of torque. The Compass gets a new six-speed automatic transmission, which replaces the CTV on most trim levels, and a flashy 6.5” touchscreen console in the Limited trim. The Patriot also gets a new six-speed transmission, and the Wrangler and Wrangler Limited remain relatively unchanged.

steps.text:
Based on my research of J.D. Power's vehicle listings and available information, here's what I found regarding SUV model availability in 2014:

## 2014 SUV Model Counts (from J.D. Power sources):

| Brand | SUV Models Listed |
|-------|-------------------|
| **Ford** | 6 models (Edge, Escape, Expedition, Expedition EL, Explorer, Flex) |
| **Jeep** | 6 models (Cherokee, Compass, Grand Cherokee, Patriot, Wrangler, Wrangler Unlimited) |
| **Chevrolet** | 5+ models (Equinox, Traverse, Tahoe, Suburban, Captiva Sport, plus HHR/TrailBlazer variants) |
| **GMC** | 5+ models (Terrain, Acadia, Yukon, Yukon XL, Envoy) |
| **Dodge** | 1 model (Journey) |
| **Cadillac** | 1 model (SRX) |
| **Nissan** | Multiple models (Murano, Pathfinder, Xterra) |
| **Lincoln** | Multiple models (MKX, Navigator, MKX Hybrid) |
| **Honda** | Multiple models (CR-V, Pilot, HR-V) |
| **Toyota** | Multiple models (RAV4, Highlander, 4Runner) |
| **Volkswagen** | 1 model (Tiguan) |

## Key Finding:

According to J.D. Power's 2014 lineup listings, **both Ford and Jeep tied for the most SUV models**, each offering approximately **6 SUV models** for the 2014 model year.

Jeep notably focused almost exclusively on SUVs in its 2014 lineup, making it one of the few manufacturers whose entire portfolio was SUV-centric. Ford offered the second-largest SUV lineup among major automakers that year.

It's important to note that J.D. Power primarily focuses on quality and dependability studies rather than counting model variety. There isn't an official J.D. Power announcement declaring which manufacturer had the "most SUV models." The above counts are derived from examining their actual 2014 vehicle listings and segment breakdowns.
